subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: What boundary should OpenClaw enforce between agent-visible errors, host exec, and persisted config writes for sandbox and exec settings?
rationale: Current source shows guarded gateway `config.patch`, an unguarded CLI `config patch` path reachable through host exec, and model-visible sandbox copy with config assignments; choosing the permanent block/provenance/allow policy requires maintainer security intent.

options.title: Harden agent-visible and exec paths
options.body: Remove protected config assignments from model-visible errors and add explicit provenance or guardrails for CLI/plugin/cron config writes before treating this issue as fixed.

options.title: Land text-only hardening
options.body: Only remove remaining model-visible sandbox config hints while explicitly accepting CLI-through-exec config writes as operator-authorized behavior.

options.title: Keep current operator hints
options.body: Document the behavior and rely on doctor/audit warnings, leaving the reported silent-mutation boundary largely unchanged.

recommendation.title: Harden agent-visible and exec paths
recommendation.body: Remove protected config assignments from model-visible errors and add explicit provenance or guardrails for CLI/plugin/cron config writes before treating this issue as fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame and adjacent sandbox/gateway config work make this the best available routing candidate for the security-boundary choice.
